skill.name: conductor-implement
skill.description: Guides AI coding agents through Conductor implementation tracks using TDD, verification checkpoints, metadata updates, and commits.
skill.summary: Run Conductor track implementation with TDD and checkpointed progress.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most static matches are false positives caused by Markdown backticks around file paths, status markers, and example text. Three findings are confirmed because the skill instructs git commits and project test execution, which can mutate the repository or execute local scripts. No prompt injection, network reconnaissance, malware intent, or data exfiltration evidence was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Broad git staging during task commits
remediation.suggestion: Replace git add -A with a required git status review and targeted staging. Ask before committing unrelated changes.
Require confirmation before running project scripts. Show the exact command source and expected scope before execution.
Label shell snippets as human-reviewed examples and avoid fenced blocks for sample dialogs when possible.

static_findings.snippet: Execute tasks from a track's implementation plan, following the workflow rules defined in `conductor
- If detailed examples are required, open `resources/implementation-playbook.md`.
- If missing: Display error and suggest running `/conductor:setup` first
For each incomplete task in plan.md (marked with `[ ]`):
- Look for lines matching `- [ ] Task X.Y: {description}`
- Update plan.md: Change `[ ]` to `[~]` for current task
- If all tasks in current phase are `[x]`:
- Run full test suite: `npm test` / `pytest` / etc.
3. Check if task is `[~]` in plan.md
- Write minimum code to make test pass
- Run tests to confirm they pass

content.value_statement: Conductor tracks can drift when tasks, tests, and metadata are updated by hand. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through TDD implementation, checkpoints, commits, and progress updates.
actual_capabilities: Checks required Conductor setup files before implementation starts.
Loads track specs, plans, metadata, product context, and workflow rules.
Selects pending tracks and advances task status through plan files.
Guides red, green, refactor cycles when TDD is enabled.
Prompts for phase approval after verification checkpoints.
Updates track metadata and completion summaries.
limitations: Requires an existing Conductor directory and valid track files.
Depends on project test commands and workflow definitions.
Can modify plans, metadata, commits, and project code during use.
Does not replace human review before phase progression.

use_cases.title: Implement a Planned Feature Track
use_cases.description: Follow a track plan from the next incomplete task through tests, implementation, commits, and metadata updates.

use_cases.title: Enforce Delivery Checkpoints
use_cases.description: Keep phase verification, approval pauses, and failure handling consistent across implementation work.

use_cases.title: Resume Interrupted Work
use_cases.description: Load current metadata, find the active task, and continue or restart work with clear options.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Track
prompt_templates.prompt: Use conductor-implement on track auth_20250115. Load context, show the next task, and ask before editing files.

prompt_templates.title: Resume Work
prompt_templates.prompt: Resume track dashboard_20250113. Read metadata, confirm the current task, and present restart or continue options.

prompt_templates.title: Implement One Task
prompt_templates.scenario: Limit work to a specific planned task.
prompt_templates.prompt: Implement only Task 2.3 in track nav-fix_20250114. Follow TDD, run scoped tests, and summarize changed files.

prompt_templates.title: Complete a Phase
prompt_templates.scenario: Run a full phase with strict checkpoints.
prompt_templates.prompt: Complete Phase 2 for track auth_20250115. Enforce verification checkpoints, commit each finished task, and stop for approval before Phase 3.

output: Validated required Conductor files and loaded workflow rules.
Selected the next incomplete task from the plan.
Prepared to write the failing test before implementation.
Loaded metadata and found the task marked in progress.
Presented options to continue, restart, or show progress first.
Paused for user direction before changing files.

output_examples.input: Finish the current phase after all tasks pass.
output: Ran phase verification and summarized test results.
Reported completed tasks and remaining approval status.
Stopped before the next phase until approval is received.

best_practices: Review the track plan and workflow settings before allowing file changes.
Use scoped tests first, then run full verification at phase boundaries.
Check git status before every commit to avoid staging unrelated work.
anti_patterns: Do not run the workflow without valid Conductor setup files.
Do not skip phase approval when verification checkpoints are configured.
Do not commit broad working tree changes without reviewing the diff.

faq.question: Does this skill run commands automatically?
faq.answer: It guides command use for tests and commits. Users should approve commands according to their tool settings.

faq.question: Can it create code changes?
faq.answer: Yes. It is designed to write tests, implement tasks, update plans, and maintain metadata.

faq.question: Does it require Conductor setup?
faq.answer: Yes. It expects conductor/product.md, conductor/workflow.md, conductor/tracks.md, and track files to exist.

faq.question: Can I use it without strict TDD?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports non-TDD workflows when the Conductor workflow allows direct implementation.

faq.question: How does it handle failures?
faq.answer: It stops on tool, test, or git failures and presents recovery options.

faq.question: Is it safe for unattended runs?
faq.answer: No. Phase checkpoints, repository changes, and project scripts need human oversight.
